selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Why does the note say some ideas from other books were included again in this treatise?
questions.answer: Because those other parts were not available there, so some important points had to be mentioned again.

questions.question: What happened to the rough draft after it was first written?
questions.answer: It was revised into another copy.

questions.question: What kind of copy was later prepared after the first rough writing?
questions.answer: A revised copy was made from the rough draft.

questions.question: What letter is the focus of that pattern?
questions.answer: The alif.

questions.question: How many alifs were counted at the beginnings of the lines?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What was that number compared with?
questions.answer: It was compared with the number value of the treatise’s title.

questions.question: Whom does the note say gave this title to the treatise?
questions.answer: Imam Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

questions.question: What number of Qur’anic verses is mentioned in the note?
questions.answer: Six thousand six hundred and sixty-six.

questions.question: What is a good one-sentence summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The note explains why some material was repeated and describes a meaningful number pattern that supports the treatise’s title and its connection to the Qur’an.

questions.question: Why were parts of The Words and The Flashes mentioned again in this treatise?
questions.answer: They were mentioned again because those other writings were not on hand where this treatise was written.

questions.question: How did that affect what was written in this treatise?
questions.answer: Important subjects from some other sections were included again.

questions.question: Was the first version polished or unfinished?
questions.answer: It was unfinished, since it is described as a rough draft.

questions.question: What kind of draft came before the revised copy?
questions.answer: A rough draft came first.

questions.question: What hidden feature was seen in his writing?
questions.answer: A fine and deep matching pattern in the letters was seen.

questions.question: What was still found in his copy even without that knowledge?
questions.answer: A deep and fine letter correspondence was found.

questions.question: How did that number connect with the treatise’s title?
questions.answer: It matched the abjad value of the title Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: Why does the note mention the total number of Qur’anic verses?
questions.answer: To connect the number pattern with the Qur’an and show another meaningful sign.

questions.question: What problem existed when this treatise was being written?
questions.answer: The other parts of the Risale-i Nur were not available in that place.

questions.question: What is the second main reason for writing down the whole treatise anyway?
questions.answer: The students there were meant to have a complete small version of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Why did they still want everything in the present treatise written down?
questions.answer: They wanted the students there to prepare a compact but complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How is the one who wrote that revised copy described?
questions.answer: He is called a blessed person.

questions.question: What careful observation was made in his copy?
questions.answer: A delicate and deep harmony in the letters was noticed.

questions.question: How many of these letters were found at line beginnings?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.

questions.question: What was the total number of those alifs?
questions.answer: Six hundred sixty-six.
